items.text: Every vehicle upon a highway of this State, subject to exceptions with respect to parked vehicles as stated in chapters 484A to 484E, inclusive, of NRS, must display lighted lamps and illuminating devices as respectively required in this chapter for different classes of vehicles: (a) At any time from one-half hour after sunset to one-half hour before sunrise; (b) At any other time when, because of insufficient light or unfavorable atmospheric conditions, persons and vehicles on the highway are not clearly discernible at a distance of 1,000 feet ahead; and (c) When directed by an official traffic control device.

Whenever a vehicle is parked or stopped upon the traveled portion of a highway or shoulder adjacent thereto, whether attended or unattended during the times mentioned in NRS 484D.100 [NRS-484D-100-1], and there is insufficient light to reveal any person or object within a distance of 1,000 feet upon such highway or roadway, such vehicle shall display lighted lamps meeting the requirements of subsection 1 [(1) appended below]. Every vehicle shall be equipped with one or more lamps which, when lighted, shall display a white or amber light visible from a distance of 500 feet to the front of the vehicle, and one or more lamps which, when lighted, shall display a red light visible from a distance of 500 feet to the rear of the vehicle. The location of such lamps shall be such that at least one such lamp is installed as near as practicable to the side of the vehicle which is closest to passing traffic.
Any lighted headlamps upon a parked vehicle shall be depressed or dimmed.

scope_reading: The selected C179824 travel cases are moving vehicle cases. The referenced parked/stopped-vehicle requirements are separately assigned to C183085 and C276263; their legal disposition cannot be inferred from the moving cases or CARLA light-state bits.
